rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Fertilizers return the three nutrients every harvest removes: nitrogenous carriers ranked by N density (urea 46%, nitrate 35%, sulphate 21%), phosphatic superphosphate made plant-available by acid treatment, and potassic KCl — combined in NPK grades whose numbers are P₂O₅/K₂O equivalents.…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: The soil's urease, not the bag's chemistry, releases urea's nitrogen.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The oldest-leaves-first rule*** - N, P and K are all mobile in the plant, so every deficiency reads on the oldest leaves - the single most useful diagnostic in the topic.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Chemical Fertilizers and the Urea Flow Sheet Plants remove nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium from soil with every harvest; fertilizers return them. The three **primary nutrients (N, P, K)** define the fertilizer types — nitrogenous, phosphatic, potassic — and the **NPK grade notation** (e.g. 15:15:15) summarises a mixed fertilizer's strengths.…  ·  ## 2. Theorem Mirror - **Nitrogenous fertilizers:** ammonium sulphate (NH₄)₂SO₄ (21% N), ammonium nitrate NH₄NO₃ (35% N), **urea CO(NH₂)₂ (46% N — the highest)**, ammonia itself. - **Phosphatic fertilizers:** superphosphate (rock phosphate Ca₃(PO₄)₂ + H₂SO₄ → soluble Ca(H₂PO₄)₂ + CaSO₄), triple superphosphate (with H₃PO₄); the treatment converts insoluble phosphate into plant-available soluble phosphate.…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Urea is the Haber process's commercial terminus - the ammonia plant's economics are often written in urea.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Types: nitrogenous ((NH4)2SO4 21% N, NH4NO3 35%, urea 46% - highest), phosphatic (superphosphate: rock phosphate + H2SO4 -> soluble Ca(H2PO4)2 + CaSO4), potassic (KCl, K2SO4). NPK grade = N : P2O5 : K2O equivalents.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Nutrient density is the currency: 46% vs 35% vs 21% N per tonne shipped decides the market.
